intro_en: In this lesson you will learn to point at places and to ask and answer "Where is the bank?", "Which floor is this?" and "How much is this?". It includes place names such as railway station, bank, post office and hospital, numbers from one hundred to ten thousand, and the yen currency. Just as Tamil says "இங்கே / அங்கே / எங்கே" (here / there / where), Japanese has ここ・そこ・あそこ・どこ, which follow the same pattern as これ・それ・あれ from the last lesson.

g03-1.explanation_en: Just as これ・それ・あれ point at things, ここ・そこ・あそこ point at places: ここ = where the speaker is ("here", இங்கே), そこ = near the listener ("there", அங்கே), あそこ = far from both ("over there", அதோ அங்கே). Just as in Tamil the "இ-" demonstrative means near and "அ-" means far, Japanese has a family of four beginnings: こ- / そ- / あ- / ど-. こちら・そちら・あちら are direction words, "this way / that way"; in shops and offices they are also used as the polite form instead of ここ・そこ・あそこ. When you introduce someone, 「こちらは 山田さんです」 = "This is Yamada-san" (இவர் யமாடா-சான்), a polite way of pointing, like the Tamil "இவர்" (this person, respectful).
g03-1.tamil_parallel_en: இங்கே வகுப்பறை "Here is the classroom" / அங்கே வங்கி "Over there is the bank" = ここは 教室です。/ あそこは 銀行です。 The Japanese こ matches Tamil "இ" (this/here), そ and あ match "அ" (that/there), and ど matches "எ" (which/where).
g03-1.formation_en: ここ / そこ / あそこ (ordinary) — こちら / そちら / あちら (polite, direction)
g03-1.pitfalls_en: When introducing someone, 「こちらは」 is much more polite than 「この人は 田中さんです」. When you say あそこ, say all of it, あそこ, not "あそ"; don't pronounce it like "அச்சோ".

g03-2.explanation_en: To say where a thing or place is, you can use the same 「N1 は N2 です」 pattern from Lesson 1: 「銀行は あそこです」 = "The bank is over there" (வங்கி அங்கே இருக்கிறது). In Tamil too we say "வங்கி அங்கே" (bank, over there) without "இருக்கிறது" (is), don't we? It is the same shortcut. The place can be ここ・そこ・あそこ, こちら・そちら・あちら, or a floor number like 五階. You can use this for people too: 「先生は 教室です」 = "The teacher is in the classroom" (ஆசிரியர் வகுப்பறையில் இருக்கிறார்).
g03-2.tamil_parallel_en: தபால் நிலையம் அங்கே "The post office is over there" = 郵便局は あそこです。 Like Tamil, which can leave out "இருக்கிறது" (is), Japanese shows "is there" with です alone.
g03-2.formation_en: N (thing / place / person) + は + place + です
g03-2.pitfalls_en: 「ここは 銀行です」 (this place is a bank) and 「銀行は ここです」 (the bank is here) are both correct, but the topic changes. If the question is "Where is the bank?", make 銀行は the topic in your answer.

g03-3.explanation_en: "Where?" = どこ; the polite form is どちら. Just as the Tamil "எ-" beginning marks a question, the Japanese ど- beginning marks question words: どれ, どの, どこ, どちら. As in Tamil, the question word stays in the place position, before です: 「駅は どこですか」 = "Where is the station?" (ரயில் நிலையம் எங்கே?). どちら also has polite meanings like "which direction" and "which country / which company": 「お国は どちらですか」 = "Which country are you from?" (உங்கள் நாடு எது?). Asking with 何ですか here is not natural.
g03-3.tamil_parallel_en: ரயில் நிலையம் எங்கே? "Where is the station?" = 駅は どこですか。 / உங்கள் நாடு எது? "Which is your country?" = お国は どちらですか。 Like the Tamil question beginning "எ-", Japanese question words start with ど-.
g03-3.formation_en: N は どこ / どちら ですか
g03-3.pitfalls_en: どちら also means "which of the two" (in later lessons). Don't ask "Which is your country?" as 「お国は 何ですか」; use どちら or どこ.

g03-4.explanation_en: Another job for の: saying which country or company made something. 「日本の 時計」 = a Japanese(-made) clock (ஜப்பானியக் கடிகாரம்), 「ソニーの カメラ」 = a Sony camera (சோனி கேமரா). In Tamil we just put the words side by side with no ending, as in "ஜப்பான் கடிகாரம்" (Japan clock) and "சோனி கேமரா" (Sony camera), but in Japanese の is required. To ask "made in which country…?", say 「どこの N ですか」, which is どこ + の. In the answer you can drop the noun, as in 「日本のです」, just like 「私のです」 in the last lesson.
g03-4.tamil_parallel_en: இது எந்த நாட்டுக் கடிகாரம்? — ஜப்பான் கடிகாரம். "Which country's clock is this? — A Japanese clock." = これは どこの 時計ですか。— 日本の 時計です。 Where Tamil puts the words side by side, Japanese needs の.
g03-4.formation_en: N1 (country / company) + の + N2 ; どこの + N ですか
g03-4.pitfalls_en: Dropping の, as in 「どこ カメラ」, is wrong; say 「どこの カメラ」. Don't confuse "whose" (誰の) with "from which country" (どこの).

g03-5.explanation_en: To ask a price, say 「N は いくらですか」 = "How much is N?" (N என்ன விலை?). The answer is number + 円 (えん): 「百円です」 = "100 yen" (நூறு யென்). Big numbers: 百 (100), 千 (1,000), 万 (10,000). Just as Tamil sounds change in "முன்னூறு" (three hundred) and "மூவாயிரம்" (three thousand), some Japanese numbers change sound: 三百 = さんびゃく, 六百 = ろっぴゃく, 八百 = はっぴゃく, 三千 = さんぜん, 八千 = はっせん. Don't say 10,000 as "ten thousand"; say 一万 (いちまん). 30,000 = 三万. Just as Indians count in lakhs (லட்சம்), Japanese people count in units of 万. 0 = ゼロ or 零 (れい).
g03-5.tamil_parallel_en: இந்தக் குடை என்ன விலை? — ஆயிரம் யென். "How much is this umbrella? — 1,000 yen." = この傘は いくらですか。— 千円です。 Also, like Tamil sound changes such as "முன்னூறு" (three hundred), Japanese numbers like 三百 (さんびゃく) change sound.
g03-5.formation_en: N は いくらですか → (number) 円です ; 百 / 千 / 万
g03-5.pitfalls_en: 四円 = よえん (not よんえん). Ten thousand = 一万; never say 「十千」. Don't put 一 before 百 / 千 (百 = ひゃく), but 一 is required before 万 (一万).

g03-6.explanation_en: To say a floor of a building, use number + 階 (かい). "Which floor?" = 何階 (なんがい). Note: in Japan the ground floor itself is 一階 (1st floor). What is called the "ground floor" in Tamil Nadu is 一階 in Japan, and our "first floor" is 二階 there. Sound changes: 一階 = いっかい, 三階 = さんがい, 六階 = ろっかい, 八階 = はっかい (or はちかい), 十階 = じゅっかい, 何階 = なんがい. To ask "Which floor is X on?", say 「X は 何階ですか」; the answer is 「三階です」. Tamil "மூன்றாவது மாடியில்" (on the third floor) uses "-இல்" (on/in), but in Japanese です alone is enough.
g03-6.tamil_parallel_en: தபால் நிலையம் எத்தனையாவது மாடி? — மூன்றாவது மாடி. "Which floor is the post office on? — The third floor." = 郵便局は 何階ですか。— 三階です。 Tamil adds "-இல்" (on), but Japanese needs only です.
g03-6.formation_en: (number) + 階 ; N は 何階ですか
g03-6.pitfalls_en: 三階 = さんがい, 何階 = なんがい; don't forget that the か sound changes to が. In Japan 一階 = the ground floor, so add one to the Indian floor number.

items.L03-q01: 駅 = えき (ரயில் நிலையம், railway station). Changing き to ぎ or adding a small っ is wrong.
items.L03-q02: 銀行 = ぎんこう (வங்கி, bank). It ends with the long sound こう; shortening it to ぎんこ or changing ぎ to き is wrong.
items.L03-q03: 病院 = びょういん (மருத்துவமனை, hospital). びょ is a single sound (with a small ょ); びよういん is 美容院 (அழகு நிலையம், beauty salon). This is a big trap!
items.L03-q04: ゆうびんきょく = 郵便局 (தபால் நிலையம், post office). The look-alike 使 (பயன்படுத்த, to use) in place of 便, and 居 in place of 局, are both traps.
items.L03-q05: たてもの = 建物 (கட்டிடம், building). 健 has an extra 亻 on the left; 勿 is only the right-hand part of 物.
items.L03-q06: What you can ask "Where?" about is a place: the toilet (கழிப்பறை). Things like a name or a number don't fit the answer "over there".
items.L03-q07: The answer is a price (三万円), so the question is いくら (என்ன விலை, how much). If it were どこ (where), the answer would be a place.
items.L03-q08: The answer is 八階 (எட்டாவது மாடி, eighth floor), so the question is 何階 (なんがい, which floor). なんさい is the word for asking someone's age.
items.L03-q09: To introduce someone politely, use こちら (இவர், this person). あそこ / そこ point at places, not people.
items.L03-q10: The place where a doctor works is 病院 (மருத்துவமனை, hospital). A doctor wouldn't be at 銀行 (வங்கி, bank) or 交番 (போலீஸ் பூத், police box).
items.L03-q11: To ask about someone's country politely, use どちら (எங்கே / எது, where / which). どなた means "who" (யார்) and doesn't fit a country.
items.L03-q12: "The bank is over there" = "What is over there is the bank" (அங்கே இருப்பது வங்கி). ここ means "here" (இங்கே), which changes the place.
items.L03-q13: "A Japanese-made clock" = "This clock is Japanese" (இந்தக் கடிகாரம் ஜப்பானியது). 日本人の would mean "belonging to a Japanese person": ownership, not where it was made.
items.L03-q14: Not the second floor but the first (ground) floor (தரை மாடி): the same meaning. The other options change the floor or deny it.
items.L03-q15: The answer is a place, "over there", so the question is どこ (எங்கே, where).
items.L03-q16: "A camera from which country" = どこの カメラ; you need の to link it to the noun.
items.L03-q17: The price of a book = 三百円 (さんびゃくえん, 300 yen). かい is for floors and さい is for ages; they don't fit a book.
items.L03-q18: After the denial いいえ, "it's not the post office" = じゃありません; then the speaker gives the right answer, 交番です (it's the police box).
items.L03-q19: Like the bank, the post office is on the second floor too, so "too" (-உம்) = も.
items.L03-q20: "What place is this?" (இது எந்த இடம்?) = ここは どこですか. The answer also uses ここは, so both people are in the same place.
items.L03-q21: The answer to an いくら (என்ன விலை, how much) question is a price: 三千円 (さんぜんえん, 3,000 yen). The others are a floor, a number and an age.
items.L03-q22: すみません、お手洗いは 何階ですか。 — topic → question word → です → か. 何階 goes in the ★ slot.
items.L03-q23: それは どこの 時計ですか。 — どこの comes before the noun. どこの goes in the ★ slot.
items.L03-q24: あの建物は 病院じゃありません。 — あの + noun, then the denial. 病院じゃ goes in the ★ slot.
items.L03-q25: ［1］ "Cameras (section) are on the fifth floor": topic は. ［2］ "Japanese camera" (ஜப்பானியக் கேமரா): の showing the country. ［3］ The answer is 八階 (eighth floor), so the question is 何階.
